title: Standard units of measurement
summary: Introduces SI units, the quantities and symbols used in electrical science, multiples and sub-multiples, and writing numbers in standard form.

sections.heading: SI units
paragraphs: Every field of science needs a set of standard units. The SI units (Système International d’Unités), published in 1960, are the modern form of the metric system.
There are seven base units, from which many other units are derived. Six are relevant to the electrotechnical industries; the seventh, the mole, is more relevant to chemistry.
bullets: Electric current: symbol I, ampere, A
Luminous intensity: symbol Iv, candela, cd

sections.heading: Common electrical units
paragraphs: Many other units used in electrical science are derived from the base units. Learn the quantity, its symbol and its unit together.
bullets: Electromotive force, E; voltage, V; potential difference, V: all measured in volts, V
Impedance, Z and reactance, X: ohm, Ω
Inductance, L: henry, H (inductive reactance is in ohms)
Capacitance, C: farad, F (capacitive reactance is in ohms)

sections.heading: Magnetic, mechanical and power units
paragraphs: Magnetic quantities, force and area have their own units, and AC power has three different kinds of power with different units.
bullets: Magnetic flux density, β: tesla, T
Power factor, p.f.: a ratio with no units
Actual power, P: watt, W or kW
Reactive power, Q: volt amps reactive, VAr or kVAr
Apparent power, S: volt amps, VA or kVA

sections.heading: Multiples and sub-multiples
paragraphs: Units are often too small or too large to use directly, for example thousandths of an ampere or millions of ohms. We multiply units up or divide them down to get practical values; the metre, for example, can be broken down into millimetres (thousandths of a metre).
Each multiple or sub-multiple has a name and symbol and is a power of 10.

sections.heading: Standard form
paragraphs: Standard form is a clear way to write large and small numbers. The number being multiplied is always less than 10, and it is multiplied by a power of 10. For example, 1000 = 10 × 10 × 10, which is written 1 × 10³.

To convert a number, move the decimal point to give a number less than 10; the number of places moved gives the power (index) of 10. For 2000 (2000.0) the point moves 3 places to the left, giving 2.0 × 10³. So 200 is written 2 × 10².
For numbers less than 1 the decimal point moves to the right, so the index is negative. For example, 0.0632 becomes 6.32 × 10⁻².

flashcards.front: What does SI stand for and when were the units published?
flashcards.back: Système International d’Unités, the modern form of the metric system, published in 1960.

flashcards.front: How many SI base units are there, and which one is more relevant to chemistry?
flashcards.back: Seven base units. The seventh, the mole, is more relevant to chemistry.

flashcards.front: SI unit and symbol for electric current
SI unit and symbol for luminous intensity
Unit and symbol for electric charge
Unit for magnetic flux and for magnetic flux density
flashcards.back: Magnetic flux Φ is measured in webers (Wb); magnetic flux density β is measured in teslas (T).

flashcards.front: What units do actual, reactive and apparent power use?
flashcards.back: Actual power: W or kW. Reactive power: VAr or kVAr. Apparent power: VA or kVA.

flashcards.front: What unit does power factor have?
flashcards.back: None. Power factor is a ratio with no units.

flashcards.front: What rule applies to the number in standard form?
flashcards.back: The number being multiplied by the power of 10 is always less than 10.

flashcards.front: Write 0.0632 in standard form and explain the negative index.
flashcards.back: 6.32 × 10⁻². The decimal point moves right to get a number less than 10, so the index is negative.

quiz.q: Which is the correct unit for magnetic flux?
quiz.why: Magnetic flux, Φ, is measured in webers (Wb); tesla is for flux density.

quiz.q: Which unit is used to measure capacitance?
quiz.why: Capacitance, C, is measured in farads, F.

quiz.q: How is 0.0632 written in standard form?
quiz.why: The decimal point moves two places to the right, giving a negative index of −2.

quiz.q: How is 200 written in standard form?
quiz.why: 200 = 2 × 10 × 10, which is 2 × 10², and the multiplied number must be less than 10.

quiz.q: What is the multiplier for the prefix micro (µ)?
What is the symbol for the prefix giga?
quiz.why: Giga has the symbol G and a multiplier of 10⁹.

quiz.q: Which quantity has no units because it is a ratio?
quiz.why: Power factor (p.f.) is a ratio with no units.

quiz.q: What is the unit of resistivity?
quiz.why: Resistivity, ρ, is measured in ohm metres, Ωm.

quiz.q: What is the unit for apparent power?
quiz.why: Apparent power, S, is measured in volt amps (VA or kVA).

quiz.q: Which is the SI base unit for temperature?
quiz.why: Temperature (symbol T) has the unit kelvin, K.
